title: Al Capone's circle, the Grand Terrace syndicate and Joe Fosco
summary: Howard went to school with Capone's brother, grew up in an Italian neighborhood, and says the syndicate was behind the Grand Terrace.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Did you ever see Capone or any of those people?
Yeah, I went to school with his baby brother.
Who was that? What was that?

Yeah. They had some kind of business. Now, I saw a truck pass about two years ago. I don't remember what it was. It had Capone on the truck. Or they strictly legitimate. His brother? Yeah. Was he always? I think so. I never heard anything about him being messed up. Just he and Hal was the two that got mixed up in there. I knew them very well. In fact, I was raised in an Italian neighborhood in Chicago. I'm going to screw with a lot of those fellas. The Anunzios, the Frasciades, Bugles.
Did Acapone come to the cars where you worked? Sure.
Would you go and talk to them when they were?

And I got news for you. That syndicate was part of the Grand Terrace. Oh, heck yeah. They owned the Grand Terrace, huh? I wouldn't say they owned it, but that was the syndicate. I see. Fox was put in front of it, you know. Ed Fox.
When Capone came to a club, would you go and talk to him, say hello to him? You could, sure. I mean, did you do it sometimes?

I spoke to him, yeah. Fosco was the one that you've seen in those days. Joe Fosco. Was he a big shot? He was in the days, the real days of Prohibition. He was a beer runner. A beer runner? Uh-huh. And later on he became one of the big guys, you know. Oh, yeah. Joe Fosco. What happened to him? Fosco? I think he's still there, huh? You know, I was up in a club, in a barrage club. In fact I was the last one to get out of there, when Hershey Miller and Nails Martin shot those two policemen, a lieutenant and a captain. When did that happen? 1919. What happened there? Some argument they had. Could King Oliver read music?
